items.question: What is the primary purpose of a flame arrestor installed on a fuel tank vent pipe?
options: To prevent sparks or external flames from entering the tank and causing an explosion
To filter out dust and debris from the air entering the tank
To monitor the pressure inside the tank during bunkering
To stop oil from overflowing onto the deck during a spill
items.explanation: Flame arrestors are safety devices that allow gas to pass but prevent the transmission of a flame to the interior of the tank, complying with fire safety standards.
items.regulation: SOLAS Chapter II-2, Regulation 4

items.question: While conducting engine room rounds, you notice a small fuel oil leak spraying onto a high-temperature exhaust manifold. What is your immediate priority action?
options: Inform the Officer of the Watch (OOW) and attempt to safely isolate the leak if possible
Clean up the spilled oil before it reaches the bilge
Go to the workshop to find a temporary patch for the pipe
Wait for the next scheduled round to see if the leak increases
items.explanation: Fuel spraying on a hot surface is a major fire hazard. Immediate notification and isolation are critical to prevent a fire.
items.regulation: ISM Code, Section 7 (Shipboard Operations)

items.question: Before entering a pump room to perform maintenance on a cargo pump, what is the most critical safety step according to the ISGOTT guidelines?
options: Verify the atmosphere is safe and the space is adequately ventilated
Ensure all tools are lubricated to prevent friction
Turn on all lights in the pump room
Check that the bilge high-level alarm is functional
items.explanation: Atmospheric testing is mandatory for enclosed spaces to check for oxygen deficiency or toxic/flammable gases before entry.
items.regulation: ISGOTT Chapter 10 / SOLAS Chapter XI-1, Reg 7

items.question: During a routine sounding of a lube oil tank, the tape shows an unexpected and rapid increase in level. What is the most likely cause?
options: Water or another fluid has leaked into the tank
The oil has expanded due to a 2-degree Celsius temperature change
The sounding pipe has become shorter due to vibration
The tank air vent is slightly blocked
items.explanation: A sudden rise in tank level usually indicates contamination, such as water ingress or a leak from an internal coil or adjacent tank.
items.regulation: STCW Table A-III/4 (Engine Room Watchkeeping)

items.question: What is the primary function of a 'wear ring' in a centrifugal cargo pump?
options: To provide a renewable leakage path between the impeller and the pump casing
To hold the mechanical seal in its correct axial position
To lubricate the shaft bearings during high-speed rotation
To prevent the pump from losing suction when the tank is low
items.explanation: Wear rings are designed to be sacrificed to protect the expensive impeller and casing from erosive wear while minimizing internal recirculation.
items.regulation: Manufacturer Guidance / Recognized Technical Standards

items.question: Why must you never use oxygen to blow dust off your clothing or to ventilate a confined space?
options: It creates an oxygen-enriched atmosphere that makes materials highly flammable
Oxygen will stain the fabric of the boiler suit
Compressed oxygen is too cold and will cause frostbite
Oxygen is a toxic gas when breathed at atmospheric pressure
items.explanation: Oxygen enrichment (above 23.5%) significantly increases the fire risk; even fire-resistant materials can burn fiercely in such conditions.
items.regulation: Code of Safe Working Practices (COSWP) Chapter 15

items.question: You find a portable electric drill with a frayed power cable. What is the correct action to take?
options: Remove the tool from service, tag it as 'Defective,' and report it to the Second Engineer
Wrap the frayed area with electrical tape and continue using it
Only use the tool if you are wearing rubber-soled safety boots
Leave it on the workbench for the next person to fix
items.explanation: Defective tools must be removed from service immediately to prevent electric shock or fire.
items.regulation: Code of Safe Working Practices (COSWP) Chapter 18

items.question: When transferring sludge to the shore reception facility, why is it important to check the temperature of the sludge?
options: To ensure the sludge is fluid enough for the pump to handle without overloading
To make sure the sludge is exactly 100 degrees Celsius to kill bacteria
To prevent the shore facility from getting cold oil
To comply with the ship's stability criteria
items.explanation: High viscosity sludge must be heated to a pumpable state, but temperature must be monitored to avoid exceeding pump limits or flashpoint risks.
items.regulation: MARPOL Annex I / Engine Room Operations

items.question: Which of these symptoms most likely indicates that a centrifugal pump is 'cavitating'?
options: Loud noise similar to pumping gravel and fluctuating discharge pressure
The pump motor starts spinning in the reverse direction
The pump casing becomes covered in thick frost
The discharge valve handle becomes difficult to turn
items.explanation: Cavitation occurs when vapor bubbles form and collapse, causing a distinct rattling noise and unstable pressure.
items.regulation: Recognized Engineering Theory / Pump Manuals

items.question: Before starting any maintenance on a fuel oil purifier, why must the 'Lock-Out Tag-Out' (LOTO) procedure be strictly followed?
options: To prevent accidental startup of the machinery while personnel are working on it.
To ensure the purifier is balanced correctly before operation.
To record the total running hours in the maintenance log.
To notify the bridge that the ship's speed must be reduced.
items.explanation: LOTO ensures that energy sources are isolated and cannot be re-energized while maintenance is being carried out, preventing injuries.
items.regulation: ISM Code, Element 7

items.question: During engine room rounds, you notice a small fuel oil leak dripping onto a hot exhaust pipe. What is your immediate action?
options: Inform the Engineer Officer of the Watch immediately and take steps to contain the leak.
Wait until the end of the watch to report it during the handover.
Wipe the oil off the pipe and check it again the next day.
Tighten the pipe connection while the engine is running at full load.
items.explanation: Oil dripping on hot surfaces is a primary cause of engine room fires. Immediate reporting and mitigation are essential for safety.
items.regulation: SOLAS Chapter II-2, Regulation 4

items.question: A Hot Work Permit is required for which of the following activities performed outside the designated workshop?
options: Oxygen-acetylene cutting of a seized bolt on the deck.
Painting a handrail in the steering gear room.
Using a manual screwdriver to tighten a terminal block.
Greasing the bearings of a ventilation fan.
items.explanation: Any activity involving open flames, sparks, or heat capable of igniting flammable materials requires a Hot Work Permit.
items.regulation: ISM Code, Safety Management System (SMS)

items.question: While cleaning the engine room bilges, you find a significant amount of sludge. Where should this sludge be disposed of?
options: Transferred to the designated sludge tank for later discharge to shore facilities or incineration.
Pumped directly overboard while the ship is more than 50 miles from land.
Mixed with the main engine fuel oil service tank immediately.
Poured down the sewage system drains.
items.explanation: Sludge must be managed according to the Ship's Waste Management Plan and MARPOL requirements, typically involving shore reception or onboard incineration.
items.regulation: MARPOL Annex I, Regulation 12

items.question: What does a 'Flame Arrestor' do when fitted on a tank vent pipe?
options: It prevents sparks or flames from entering the tank while allowing vapors to pass.
It stops the flow of liquid if the tank is overfilled.
It measures the concentration of flammable gas inside the tank.
It automatically extinguishes fires using CO2 gas.
items.explanation: Flame arrestors are safety devices that allow gas to pass but prevent the transmission of a flame into the tank by dissipating heat.
items.regulation: SOLAS Chapter II-2, Regulation 4.5.3

items.question: While on duty in the engine room, you notice a small fuel oil leak spraying from a pressurized pipe onto a hot exhaust manifold. What is your immediate first action?
options: Call the bridge immediately to report the leak.
Attempt to tighten the leaking connection with a wrench.
Alert the Duty Engineer and prepare to activate emergency stops if instructed.
Get a fire extinguisher and stand by near the leak.
items.explanation: Safety and communication are paramount; reporting to the officer in charge ensures the pump can be stopped before an ignition occurs.
items.regulation: SOLAS Chapter II-2, Regulation 4 (Probability of Ignition)

items.question: Before starting any electric arc welding task on a steel bulkhead, which of the following is a critical safety requirement for the immediate area?
options: Ensure the surrounding area is cleared of all combustible materials.
Paint the bulkhead with a fresh coat of primer to prevent oxidation.
Turn off all ventilation to prevent the spread of fumes.
Ensure the welding machine is plugged into a lighting circuit.
items.explanation: Hot work requires the removal of combustibles to prevent fire spread through heat conduction or sparks.
items.regulation: ISM Code, Section 7 (Shipboard Operations / Safety Management System)

items.question: A Pumpman is preparing a centrifugal cargo pump for operation. Why is it essential to 'prime' the pump before starting?
options: To cool down the mechanical seal.
To remove air or vapor and ensure the impeller is submerged in liquid.
To increase the pressure in the discharge line.
To verify that the direction of rotation is correct.
items.explanation: Centrifugal pumps cannot move air; they must be filled with liquid (primed) to create the necessary pressure differential.
items.regulation: ISGOTT Chapter 12 (Pump Room Safety and Operations)

items.question: A motor requires maintenance, and a Lock-Out Tag-Out (LOTO) procedure is initiated. Who is the only person permitted to remove the safety lock?
options: The Chief Engineer.
The person who originally applied the lock.
The Engine Cadet on duty.
The Wiper cleaning the area.
items.explanation: Standard safety protocol dictates that only the authorized person who applied the lock may remove it to ensure they are clear of the danger zone.
items.regulation: Code of Safe Working Practices (COSWP) Chapter 15

items.question: During engine room rounds, you notice a pressure gauge on a lubricating oil filter is showing a significantly higher differential pressure than normal. What does this likely indicate?
options: The oil temperature is too high.
The filter element is becoming clogged.
The pump is running too slowly.
The oil tank is nearly empty.
items.explanation: Differential pressure increases when a filter is restricted or clogged, indicating a need for cleaning or switching.
items.regulation: STCW Table A-III/4 (Monitoring and operating machinery systems)

items.question: Which of the following describes the correct procedure for entering a pump room on a tanker?
options: Enter alone as long as you have a handheld radio.
Ensure ventilation is running, check atmosphere, and follow the permit-to-work system.
Open all valves first before entering to ensure airflow.
Leave the door open for 5 minutes and then proceed.
items.explanation: Pump rooms are enclosed spaces with high risk of gas accumulation; strict entry protocols and ventilation are required.
items.regulation: ISGOTT Chapter 10 (Enclosed Space Entry)

items.question: While checking the main engine lubrication system, you find the oil level is low. What is the most important factor to verify before adding make-up oil?
options: That the oil brand is the same as the one used in the auxiliary engines.
That the oil grade and specification match the existing oil in the sump.
That the oil is heated to at least 80 degrees Celsius.
That the oil has been filtered through a 15ppm separator.
items.explanation: Mixing incompatible grades or incorrect specifications can lead to loss of lubrication properties or chemical reactions.
items.regulation: STCW Table A-III/4 (Engine Room Watchkeeping)

items.question: When using a portable electric drill in a damp area of the engine room, which safety device is essential to prevent electric shock?
options: A heavy-duty extension cord.
A Residual Current Device (RCD) or Ground Fault Circuit Interrupter (GFCI).
A pair of leather gloves.
A wooden stool to stand on.
items.explanation: RCDs/GFCIs protect personnel by cutting power instantly if a leakage to ground is detected.
items.regulation: Code of Safe Working Practices (COSWP) Chapter 15

items.question: While performing engine room rounds, you notice a fuel oil pipe vibration that was not present before. What is the most appropriate immediate action?
options: Report the change to the Officer of the Watch immediately.
Wait until the end of the watch to record it in the logbook.
Attempt to tighten the pipe supports while the engine is running.
Ignore it if there is no visible leakage.
items.explanation: Any new or unusual vibration in high-pressure systems can lead to fatigue failure and fire; immediate reporting is required by safety management protocols.
items.regulation: STCW Code Table A-III/4 (Monitoring Engine Room)

items.question: Which specific safety document must be issued and signed before a Fitter begins electric arc welding on a bulkhead in the engine workshop?
options: Hot Work Permit
Enclosed Space Entry Permit
Cold Work Permit
Cargo Handling Permit
items.explanation: Arc welding involves high temperatures and sparks, categorizing it as Hot Work, which requires a formal risk assessment and permit.
items.regulation: ISGOTT Chapter 9 / ISM Code

items.question: When taking soundings of a lube oil tank, why is it important to ensure the tape is wiped clean before and after the measurement?
options: To prevent cross-contamination of oils and ensure an accurate reading.
To prevent the tape from rusting.
To make the tape easier to wind back into the reel.
To comply with the Garbage Management Plan.
items.explanation: Cleanliness prevents introducing impurities into the lube system and ensures the oil cut is clearly visible for accuracy.
items.regulation: IMO Model Course 7.04 (Engine Room Watchkeeping)

items.question: A Pumpman is preparing a centrifugal cargo pump for operation. What must be done to prevent the pump from overheating during startup?
options: Ensure the pump is primed and the suction valve is open.
Keep the discharge valve fully closed for at least 30 minutes.
Run the pump dry for 5 minutes to warm up the seals.
Disconnect the cooling water to the pedestal.
items.explanation: Centrifugal pumps require fluid to dissipate heat generated by the impeller; running dry or without flow causes rapid heat buildup and seal failure.
items.regulation: ISGOTT Section 12.1 (Pumping Operations)

items.question: According to MARPOL Annex I, what is the maximum oil content allowed for treated bilge water to be discharged overboard while a ship is en route?
options: 15 parts per million (ppm)
100 parts per million (ppm)
0 parts per million (ppm)
50 parts per million (ppm)
items.explanation: MARPOL Regulation 14 prohibits discharge of oil or oily mixtures into the sea unless the oil content does not exceed 15 ppm.
items.regulation: MARPOL Annex I, Regulation 14

items.question: When applying Lock-Out Tag-Out (LOTO) on a fuel pump for maintenance, who should keep the key to the padlock?
options: The person performing the maintenance work.
The Chief Engineer only.
The First Mate on the bridge.
The Wiper who cleaned the area.
items.explanation: To ensure personal safety, the person working on the equipment must maintain control of the isolation device to prevent accidental energization.
items.regulation: Code of Safe Working Practices (COSWP) Chapter 15

items.question: During a routine inspection, you find an oily rag lying on top of a hot steam pipe. Why is this a major fire hazard?
options: Spontaneous combustion or ignition due to the high temperature of the pipe.
The rag will block the heat radiation from the pipe.
The oil will evaporate and cause a toxic gas hazard.
The pipe will corrode faster under the rag.
items.explanation: Oily rags are prone to spontaneous combustion, and contact with hot surfaces significantly increases the risk of ignition.
items.regulation: SOLAS Chapter II-2, Regulation 4 (Probability of Ignition)

items.question: If a pump's mechanical seal begins to leak excessively during cargo discharge, what is the Pumpman's first priority?
options: Stop the pump and notify the Cargo Officer.
Tighten the seal while the pump is rotating.
Increase the pump speed to force the leak to stop.
Pour water over the seal to cool it down.
items.explanation: Excessive leakage indicates seal failure, which can lead to pump room flooding or fire if the cargo is flammable. The pump must be stopped immediately.
items.regulation: ISGOTT Chapter 12 / STCW Code Table A-III/7

items.situation: You are a Motorman on watch at night. While checking the auxiliary engine, you notice the high-pressure fuel pipe for Cylinder No. 3 is vibrating excessively and has a hairline crack leaking a fine stream of fuel onto the hot exhaust manifold. There is no fire yet, but smoke is starting to form.
items.question: What do you do? Explain your actions in order.
key_steps: Immediately activate the emergency stop for the auxiliary engine.
Inform the Duty Engineer and the Bridge that an engine has been emergency stopped.
Use a CO2 extinguisher locally if a flash fire occurs during coast-down.
Close the fuel supply valves to the engine.
Ensure the 'sheathed' pipe system or spray shields are properly inspected for failure.
items.critical_step: Immediately activate the emergency stop for the auxiliary engine.
items.regulation: SOLAS Chapter II-2, Regulation 4 (Flammability of Oils)

items.question: During a bunkering operation, you notice a small fuel leak near a flange that your supervisor has not yet seen. What is your immediate course of action and reporting procedure?
key_steps: Immediately signal the person in charge (PIC) to stop the bunkering operation
Place a drip tray or use sawdust/absorbent pads to contain the localized spill
Formally report the leak to the Watch Engineer or Chief Engineer
Assist in tightening the flange or replacing the gasket as directed once pressure is relieved
items.critical_step: Immediately signal to stop the bunkering operation to prevent a minor leak from becoming a major pollution incident.
items.regulation: MARPOL Annex I, SOPEP (Shipboard Oil Pollution Emergency Plan)

items.situation: A Fitter is instructed to weld a bracket in the steering gear room. Upon arrival, you note that the space is cluttered with oily rags and the ventilation seems insufficient, but the job is marked as 'Urgent' by the Second Engineer.
items.question: What do you do? Explain your actions in order.
key_steps: Refuse to start work until a valid Hot Work Permit is issued
Remove all flammable materials and oily rags from the vicinity
Ensure a fire watch is present with a portable extinguisher
Verify that the atmosphere has been tested and is safe for work
Ensure adequate ventilation is active during the entire process
items.critical_step: Refuse to start work until a valid Hot Work Permit is issued
items.regulation: ISM Code Element 7 (Development of Plans for Shipboard Operations)

items.situation: During a bunkering operation, you are the Oiler stationed at the manifold. You observe that the pressure gauge on the bunker line is rising rapidly beyond the agreed delivery pressure, and the hose appears to be under extreme tension.
items.question: What do you do? Explain your actions in order.
key_steps: Signal the bunker barge to stop pumping immediately
Close the vessel's manifold valve only after the pump has stopped to avoid surge
Notify the Chief Engineer and the Bunker Station Officer
Check all tank levels and valves to ensure no blockage caused the pressure spike
Inspect the bunker hose for any signs of physical damage or bulging
items.critical_step: Signal the bunker barge to stop pumping immediately
items.regulation: MARPOL Annex I (Prevention of Pollution during Bunkering)

items.situation: You are a Fitter required to enter a fuel oil tank for internal inspection. The tank has been ventilated for 24 hours. The O2 meter shows 20.9%, but the Chief Engineer has not yet signed the Enclosed Space Entry Permit.
items.question: What do you do? Explain your actions in order.
key_steps: Wait outside the tank and do not enter under any circumstances
Verify that a standby person is posted at the entrance with communication gear
Confirm that the permit is fully authorized and signed by the Master or Chief Engineer
Perform a final personal gas test at the tank opening
Ensure all mechanical and electrical isolations (LOTO) are confirmed
items.critical_step: Wait outside the tank and do not enter under any circumstances
items.regulation: IMO Resolution A.1050(27) (Revised Recommendations for Entering Enclosed Spaces)

items.question: You are assisting a Fitter with hot work in the engine room. You notice he has not placed a fire watch or moved nearby flammable rags. How do you handle this?
key_steps: Use the 'Stop Work Authority' to halt the task immediately
Point out the specific fire hazards (rags and lack of watch) to the Fitter
Ensure the Fire Permit requirements are fully implemented before restarting
Report the safety non-conformity to the Second Engineer
items.critical_step: Halt the task immediately using Stop Work Authority until hazards are mitigated.
items.regulation: ISM Code - Safety Management System (Section 7: Development of Plans for Shipboard Operations)

items.question: As a Motorman, you are handing over the watch to your relief. What information must be included to ensure a safe transition?
key_steps: State all current machinery status and any ongoing maintenance tasks
Report any unusual sounds, vibrations, or temperature fluctuations observed
Confirm the levels of all service tanks and waste tanks
Clearly communicate any standing orders or specific instructions from the Chief Engineer
items.critical_step: Clearly communicate any ongoing maintenance tasks and machinery abnormalities.
items.regulation: STCW Code Section A-VIII/2 - Watchkeeping arrangements and principles to be observed

items.question: During a heavy lifting operation in the engine room, you see a junior rating standing directly under a suspended load. What is your responsibility?
key_steps: Verbally command the rating to move out of the danger zone immediately
Signal the crane/hoist operator to stop movement
Brief the team on 'Line of Fire' hazards before resuming
Ensure the area is properly cordoned off with safety tape
items.critical_step: Verbally command the rating to move and signal the operator to stop movement.
items.regulation: Code of Safe Working Practices for Merchant Seafarers (COSWP) - Chapter 19
